name: Opus 5 unrestricted
strategy: Concentrated bet on the 2026 oil-supply-shock rotation: ~53% effective energy exposure via 2x ERX plus refiner MPC, carried by low-correlation healthcare/financials/defense longs, hedged by a short in oil-taxed consumer discretionary and a small stopped short-DOGE perp, with 8% cash at 4%.

positions.thesis: 2x Energy Select — the core. 32 points buys 64% effective XLE exposure. The trade is the dislocation: on 29 July crude gapped +6.2% (WTI $84.18, Brent $89.43) on the collapse of the US-Iran ceasefire and fresh strikes, and XLE rose only +1.88%. Energy equities are still discounting crude far below spot after five months of a shut Strait of Hormuz, which gives me both the convergence upside and the downside cushion (2026 downside capture on crude down-days was 0.27x — equities cannot hand back a move they never made). XLE is the #1 sector of 2026 at +37.3% YTD and +9.02% in July while XLK fell 6.81%, the widest monthly split since January 2022. ERX printed +3.78% against XLE's +1.88% — exactly 2.0x, no measurable decay. The -30% stop caps this leg at 9.6% of NAV and corresponds to roughly a -15% XLE break.

Healthcare — the ballast that makes the energy concentration carryable. -0.07 correlation to XLE and 0.22 to SPY at only 13.7% annualised vol, +25.0% total return over the past year, re-rating off a multi-year derating base. State Street has just upgraded healthcare from neutral to positive for Q3 2026 on drug-pipeline wins, so the trend has fresh institutional sponsorship. Deliberately unlevered rather than 3x CURE: the whole point of this leg is that it does not add variance.

The funding short and the cleanest statement of the thesis: an oil shock is a consumer tax, and Brent at $89 with Hormuz shut is a large one. Raised from 13% because it now does double duty — 23.2% AMZN plus 15.7% TSLA means 39% of this ETF sits at the intersection of the consumer squeeze and the AI-valuation de-rating that dragged XLK down 6.81% in July. XLY is $111.61 with a -0.54% total return over the past year at only 17% vol, and its -0.38 daily correlation to XLE makes it additive to the energy core rather than an offset. Also my only broad protection if the market breaks. An ETF, so no earnings-gap squeeze risk; 3% APR borrow; -18% stop if the consumer trade turns.

Refining/crack-spread leg, sized up into the 4 August print — the only near-dated catalyst in the book. Consensus Q2 EPS of ~$11-12 is +184-199% y/y on ~$42bn revenue, with management having front-loaded ~40% of annual turnarounds into Q1 specifically to run 2.99mb/d at ~94% utilisation into this window. The $301.59 average price target is stale and sits below the $308.72 spot while the two most recent revisions are Goldman $376 and TD Cowen $357. Cracks are a distinct driver from crude beta (-0.16 correlation to SPY), so this is not simply more ERX. Sized at 16% with a -25% stop, which caps single-name earnings-gap damage at 4.0% of NAV.

Small convexity leg on an engine asymmetry that still holds: short perps pay zero funding while long perps pay leverage x 10% APR, so the leverage here is free. DOGE is $0.0702, down 0.6% on the day, still pinned at the bottom of its range with no participation in any crypto bounce — the worst cross-sectional performer in the asset class. Loss is hard-capped at the 3% margin; the -50% stop and +90% take-profit (DOGE -30%) give roughly 1.8:1. Trimmed one point to fund the energy core.

reassessment_note:
Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): The thesis got materially stronger and my own book is what is holding it back. Since 27 July the account has made +0.36% while the mandate's core driver went vertical — crude +6.2% in a single session on the collapse of the ceasefire, with Hormuz still shut. The energy legs did their job (ERX +3.78% on the day) and the diversifiers ate the gains: AAPL -0.56%, XLV -0.61%, RTX -1.52%. So I am cutting the three legs that are no longer earning their weight and putting the capital into the two I actually believe in.

CUT AAPL (7% to 0). It was bought as a hedge against the tech unwind reversing. It has stopped being that hedge: XLK fell 6.81% in July while AAPL made an all-time high and crossed $5trn. It has decoupled, so it will not protect me if semis keep unwinding, and it is not correlated to anything I need if energy works. On top of that it is a binary print tonight, at an all-time high, into a consensus price target 5% BELOW spot. That is a coin flip I am not paid to take.

CUT RTX (7% to 0). This is the cleanest sell signal in the packet. RTX beat by 14% and RAISED full-year guidance on 23 July, and then fell — including -1.52% on the day crude gapped 6% on fresh Middle East strikes. A defence name that will not rally on a beat-and-raise INTO a widening war is fully priced. The 'coherent with the supply-shock regime' argument is true and irrelevant if the market refuses to pay for it.

CUT XLF (11% to 0). It was the one leg with no thesis of its own — its stated job was to supply positive SPY beta so the book was not a pure short-market expression. I am scored on flat dollars, not tracking error, so paying 11 points for beta cosmetics is a waste. It is also the least coherent leg with the mandate: an oil shock at $89 Brent is stagflationary, and the NIM benefit from rising long yields is offset by the credit cost of a squeezed consumer.

ADD ERX 22% to 32% (64% effective XLE). The single best piece of information I found is that XLE rose 1.88% on a 6.2% crude day. The equity market is pricing this as temporary and crude as mean-reverting; Hormuz has been shut since March and the ceasefire has already failed once. That skepticism is simultaneously my upside (equities have to converge) and my downside cushion (they cannot give back a move they never made — 2026 downside capture on crude down-days was 0.27x). ERX again realised exactly 2.0x with no decay, so I am getting the leverage cleanly. Stop stays at -30%, which caps this leg at 9.6% of NAV and corresponds to roughly a -15% XLE break.

ADD MPC 9% to 16%. Highest-conviction single name and the only near-dated catalyst I own: 4 August, consensus EPS +184-199% y/y on record cracks, with management having pulled 40% of annual turnarounds into Q1 specifically to run at 94% utilisation into this window. The sell-side average PT of $301.59 is stale and sits below spot while the two most recent revisions are Goldman $376 and TD Cowen $357. Crack spreads are a genuinely different driver from crude beta (-0.16 correlation to SPY), so this is not just more ERX. I am sizing it BEFORE the print because the print is the reason. The -25% stop caps the leg at 4.0% of NAV, which is the price of admission for a stock up 71% YTD.

ADD XLY SHORT 13% to 17%. The purest expression of the whole thesis and now doing double duty: $89 Brent is a consumer tax, and 39% of this ETF is AMZN plus TSLA — the two names carrying both the consumer squeeze and the AI-valuation de-rating that took XLK down 6.81% in July. At -0.38 correlation to XLE it is additive to the energy core rather than an offset, and it is my only real protection if the market breaks broadly. An ETF, so no single-name squeeze risk; 3% borrow; stop stays -18%.

HOLD XLV at 20%. This is what lets me carry an 80% effective energy position. -0.07 correlation to XLE, 13.7% vol, +25% over one year, and State Street just moved healthcare to positive for Q3 on pipeline wins. Still unlevered on purpose — I do not want leverage on the ballast.

HOLD DOGE short 3% at 3x. Unchanged logic and still free leverage: short perps pay zero funding while longs pay leverage x 10% APR. DOGE is at $0.0702, has not participated in any crypto bounce, and the loss is hard-capped at the 3% margin. Trimmed a point to fund the core.

RISK FRAME. Effective energy exposure goes from ~53% to 80% of NAV. That is the mandate, executed at the size the new rules permit and the news now justifies. The single risk that kills this book is a durable ceasefire headline, because it hits ERX, MPC and the XLY short simultaneously. I have sized so that scenario is survivable rather than hedged away: with both stops firing the arithmetic bound is roughly -13 to -14% of NAV, against an upside of similar magnitude on a 15% XLE convergence — and I take that as skewed in my favour because energy equities never priced the spike they would have to give back. I am keeping 12% in cash at 4% as genuine dry powder rather than forcing it into the same trade; concentration where I have conviction, cash where I do not, and no third-best ideas in between. Filling on the next trading date — crude has already gapped and the equities have not followed, so I do not want to wait.
novelty: I manage only a Round-3 book in this experiment — there is no Round-2 book of mine for this to overlap with, so the <50% same-direction gross-weight overlap constraint is satisfied vacuously; for the record, versus my own prior Round-3 book this rebalance removes three of eight legs entirely (AAPL, RTX, XLF = 25 points of gross) and materially resizes three more.
research_notes: Searched/fetched live market data on 2026-07-29/30. Energy equities are still discounting crude far below spot — the convergence trade is long the equities, not long crude, and it is exactly the asymmetry my original thesis was built on. ERX printed +3.78% on XLE's +1.88% — clean 2.0x tracking, no decay ($92.04). XLV $166.24, +25.0% 1yr, and State Street just upgraded healthcare from neutral to POSITIVE for Q3 on drug-pipeline wins — the ballast leg is confirmed. XLY $111.61 and falling, -0.54% total return over 1yr, top holdings AMZN 23.2% + TSLA 15.7% = the two names most exposed to both a consumer squeezed by $89 Brent and the ongoing tech de-rating. AGAINST my existing legs: XLK fell -6.81% in July (steepest XLK/XLE monthly split since Jan 2022) on AI-valuation and semi fears, yet AAPL is at an all-time high having just crossed $5trn, with a consensus PT of $321.66 that sits 5% BELOW the $338.19 spot — and it prints tonight, 30 July, after the close. RTX beat big on 23 July ($1.89 vs $1.66) and raised FY guidance to $7.10-7.25, and the stock has gone DOWN since, -1.52% on 29 July, straight through a week of Middle East re-escalation. DOGE $0.0702, -0.6% on the day, still pinned at the lows with no participation in any crypto bounce.
